I've created an app. Then added an authorized user, e.g.

    addAuthorizedUser("garrett")
    deployApp()

The app then becomes password protected, as advertised in the Getting Started Guide. And my password works. Hooray! Next, I remove the authorized user.

    removeAuthorizedUser("garrett")
    deployApp()

This user's password no longer works. Hooray, again! But the app is still password protected and now no one is authorized to access it.

    authorizedUsers()
    ##    user  hash
    ## 1 FALSE FALSE

Is there a way to make the app accessible to _everyone_ once more?

Thanks,
Garrett

The problem with that approach is that the shinyapps package does not get installed on your application instances when you deploy your application because the shinyapps package itself is not a detected dependency of your code.

To workaround this you should put the CAfile in your application directory and reference it via its relative path e.g:

RCurlOptions cainfo = "cacert.pem"

Or you could incude the CAcert  file in Rbitcoin package, as we have done in shinyapps:

RCurlOptions cainfo = system.file("cert", "cacert.pem", package = "Rbitcoin")

However, the underlying issue is that the CACert shipping with RCurl is out of date. My other suggestion would be to reach out to the RCurl package maintainer and see if he will update it, and push a new version to CRAN.

-Andy

Hello! I think I may have found a problem that some other windows users might encounter when trying to deploy an app that sources/loads a file from your disc. I had an app that behaved well when running locally, but it depended on loading a .Rdata file located somewhere like "C:/workingdirectory/Myapp/data/myfile.Rdata". I ran deployApp() and it went smoothly but  the app wouldn't work (it had that grayish dissapointing look). I figured it had something to do with how I was trying to load so I tried a few things with no success until I decided to add this bit of code to download the data from dropbox instead:

diputados.m<-repmis::source_DropboxData("diputados.csv","qr3scz6dwx3wyrl",sep=",",header=TRUE)
senadores.m<-repmis::source_DropboxData("senadores.csv","0dguhsu56s4umu5",sep=",",header=TRUE)

And then it worked fine, as you can see here in MYAPP <https://asiamkt.shinyapps.io/App-2/>. I wonder what the correct way of pathing is. I imagine is something like load("~/myusername/Shinyapps/myapp/data/myfile.Rdata") but I couldn't quite figure it out. I imagine any other windows users are gonna be confused as to why their app isn't running on the web even though locally it runs perfect and something like this might be the problem.

Cheers

Hi,

You should always use a relative path name when accessing your applications data or other files. The relative path name should be from the application directory.

In other words, if your local file is located at "C:\Documents\MyApp\mydata.csv", you should do something like this:

setwd("C:\Documents\MyApp")
runApp()
deployApp()

Inside your source files you can reference "mydata.csv" directly and it will work both remotely and locally.

-Andy
